Subject: Exploring Redwood plans for pilot -> production

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team liked the predictable latency and the KV cache behavior. We're kicking off a 6-week internal pilot and want to understand the best path to production. Two quick questions: 1) For a mid-sized engineering team (10 engineers, ~200k tokens/day), is seat-based pricing or throughput (tokens) likely to be lower-cost for the first 12 months? 2) If we buy reserved capacity and later decide to downscale, what does the downgrade/grandfathering look like?

Attached is a usage snapshot for the pilot so you can see the token profile. Procurement will be looped on follow-ups.

Appreciate any quick guidance — can also hop on a call.

Best,
Maria

StellarOps Inc

Hi Maria — great to meet you yesterday. Short answers first, details below and I've attached a short pricing brief.

1) For 200k tokens/day with 10 engineers, a hybrid approach typically wins: reserved baseline for predictable p95 latency (saves ~15-25% on heavy inference patterns) + metered overage for spiky scoping.
2) Downgrade/grandfathering: we support step-downs after a 30-day notice window; we commonly offer a 3–6 month credit smoothing window to avoid cliff costs for early adopters depending on commit length.

If you want a simple rule of thumb: if you expect steady monthly token consumption > 3M tokens, reserved capacity with a small commit looks better. Below that, metered is lower friction.

I attached a one-page brief (RB-pricing-2027Q2.pdf) and can schedule Ben from commercial to propose a term sheet for procurement. Do you want us to draft a 12-month commitment scenario with a 20% discount and migration credit?

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop

Hi Maria / Team — quick technical/pricing note to make the tradeoffs concrete so procurement can model cost: 

Summary math (illustrative, based on your 200k tokens/day snapshot):
- Metered: ~6M tokens/month; at list metered rate = $0.0006/token => monthly ~$3,600.
- Reserved (small baseline): commit to capacity that covers 70% of expected tokens (4.2M tokens/month) yields ~18% unit discount via reserved pricing => monthly ~$3,000 + metered overage for spikes.
- Example blended: reserved baseline + 30% metered results in ~10–12% savings vs pure metered and protects p95 latency.

On downgrade/grandfathering: 
- We can set a formal clause: single annual step-down allowed (or one in a 12-month commitment) with 60-day notice. Step-down can reduce reserved baseline up to 25% with no penalty; larger reductions convert to credits spread over 3 months.
- For migration bursts: we propose migration credits as platform credits (not cash refunds) applied to the invoice following migration. This avoids complexity with seat/throughput accounting and is standard.

Operational notes: 
- If you need to ensure absolute no-risk rollback (i.e., cancel and return to purely metered with full refund), we can offer a pilot protection: trial pilot credits that guarantee a one-time full credit up to $10k if you decide not to proceed within 60 days.

Next steps I suggest: Ben to produce a short term sheet that includes the above bullets; Lauren to route for legal to bake the step-down language; Maria / Procurement to confirm expected steady-state monthly tokens. Once we have numbers we can produce an exact DocuSign-ready amendment.
